title: the rendered screen, read once over HTTP
asserts: a caller that only wants to LOOK at a session gets the parsed grid rather than a byte log it would have to replay: text/plain by default, the screen frame's own styled rows under ?json=1 carrying the cols/rows they were rendered at, scrollback history above the screen at NEGATIVE row indices so the visible rows keep the 0 … rows-1 a screen frame uses, a 404 for an id the core never held, and a 409 once the pty is gone — which is what tells a caller to fall back to the stored scrollback on purpose rather than read an empty grid as an empty session.

steps.note: a CLI naming its own window; the read reports that name, and it has to survive the core ADOPTING it as the session title — a title stolen by the adoption would leave every peek at a long-running session reporting a nameless window
the pty round trip plus the parse; nothing about this read is a subscription, so there is no frame to wait on instead
the default body is the screen as a human reads it: no JSON envelope, no escapes, no replay
cols/rows are the grid these rows were LAID OUT at, and `rows` stays the grid height rather than doubling as the length of `lines` — the two differ the moment history is asked for

send.data: ECHO scrolled row 0ECHO scrolled row 1ECHO scrolled row 2ECHO scrolled row 3ECHO scrolled row 4ECHO scrolled row 5ECHO scrolled row 6ECHO scrolled row 7ECHO scrolled row 8ECHO scrolled row 9ECHO scrolled row 10ECHO scrolled row 11ECHO scrolled row 12ECHO scrolled row 13ECHO scrolled row 14ECHO scrolled row 15ECHO scrolled row 16ECHO scrolled row 17ECHO scrolled row 18ECHO scrolled row 19ECHO scrolled row 20ECHO scrolled row 21ECHO scrolled row 22ECHO scrolled row 23ECHO scrolled row 24ECHO scrolled row 25ECHO scrolled row 26ECHO scrolled row 27ECHO scrolled row 28ECHO scrolled row 29

steps.note: 30 lines into a 24-row grid, so there is history above the screen to ask for
history is prepended at -5 … -1, which leaves the visible grid at exactly 0 … 23: one client decoder reads a peek and a live screen frame alike, and there is no ambiguity about where history ends
the text body flows the same history in above the same screen
an id the core never held is a 404 — a distinct answer from the 409 below, because only one of the two means there is a stored scrollback worth falling back to

the screen is live state: it died with the pty. A 200 with an empty grid would be indistinguishable from a session that simply has nothing on it, and the caller would never know to read the stored bytes instead. The byte-log read that 409 points at is not asserted here because it is not a route both cores serve: the Swift core only relays /scrollback to a daemon, it answers none itself
